canonical.quote: (This should not exclude the possibility of implementing TFTP on top of other datagram protocols.)
canonical.obligation: An implementation is permitted to run TFTP over datagram protocols other than UDP.

canonical.quote: The only thing it can do is read and write files (or mail) from/to a remote server.  It cannot list directories
canonical.obligation: An implementation provides only file read and write operations, with no directory listing and no user authentication.

canonical.quote: In common with other Internet protocols, it passes 8 bit bytes of data.
canonical.obligation: File data is carried as 8-bit bytes.

canonical.quote: netascii (This is ascii as defined in "USA Standard Code for Information Interchange" [1] with the modifications specified in "Telnet Protocol Specification" [3].)
canonical.obligation: The netascii transfer mode is 8-bit ASCII per USAS X3.4-1968 with the Telnet Protocol Specification modifications.

canonical.quote: octet (This replaces the "binary" mode of previous versions of this document.) raw 8 bit bytes
canonical.obligation: The octet transfer mode carries raw 8-bit bytes and replaces the older "binary" mode name.

canonical.quote: (The mail mode is obsolete and should not be implemented or used.)
canonical.obligation: An implementation must not implement or use the mail transfer mode.

canonical.quote: Additional modes can be defined by pairs of cooperating hosts.
canonical.obligation: An implementation may define additional transfer modes by bilateral agreement with a cooperating peer.

canonical.quote: Reference [4] (section 4.2) should be consulted for further valuable directives and suggestions on TFTP.
canonical.obligation: An implementation must also apply the TFTP directives of RFC 1123 section 4.2.

canonical.quote: Any transfer begins with a request to read or write a file, which also serves to request a connection.
canonical.obligation: Every transfer is initiated by an RRQ or WRQ, which simultaneously requests the connection.

canonical.quote: If the server grants the request, the connection is opened and the file is sent in fixed length blocks of 512 bytes.
canonical.obligation: On granting a request the server opens the connection and the file is transferred in fixed-length 512-byte blocks.

canonical.quote: Each data packet contains one block of data
canonical.obligation: A DATA packet carries exactly one block of data.

canonical.quote: must be acknowledged by an acknowledgment packet before the next packet can be sent
canonical.obligation: The sender must receive an ACK for a DATA packet before sending the next DATA packet (lock-step).

canonical.quote: A data packet of less than 512 bytes signals termination of a transfer.
canonical.obligation: A DATA packet with fewer than 512 data bytes signals the end of the transfer.

canonical.quote: the intended recipient will timeout and may retransmit his last packet (which may be data or an acknowledgment)
canonical.obligation: On timeout a party may retransmit its last packet, which causes the peer to retransmit the lost packet; constrained by RFC 1123 4.2.3.1.

canonical.quote: The sender has to keep just one packet on hand for retransmission
canonical.obligation: An implementation need buffer only one outstanding packet for retransmission.

canonical.quote: Most errors cause termination of the connection.
canonical.obligation: An error terminates the connection except in the one case singled out below.

canonical.quote: An error is signalled by sending an error packet.
canonical.obligation: An implementation signals an error by sending an ERROR packet.

canonical.quote: This packet is not acknowledged, and not retransmitted
canonical.obligation: An ERROR packet is neither acknowledged nor retransmitted.

canonical.quote: (i.e., a TFTP server or user may terminate after sending an error message)
canonical.obligation: A server or user may terminate immediately after sending an ERROR packet.

canonical.quote: Therefore timeouts are used to detect such a termination when the error packet has been lost.
canonical.obligation: An implementation uses timeouts to detect a peer termination whose ERROR packet was lost.

canonical.quote: Errors are caused by three types of events: not being able to satisfy the request ... receiving a packet which cannot be explained
canonical.obligation: An implementation raises an error on unsatisfiable request, unexplainable/malformed packet, or loss of a needed resource.

canonical.quote: TFTP recognizes only one error condition that does not cause termination, the source port of a received packet being incorrect.
canonical.obligation: An incorrect source port on a received packet is the only error that does not terminate the connection.

canonical.quote: In this case, an error packet is sent to the originating host.
canonical.obligation: On receiving a packet with an incorrect source port, an ERROR packet is sent to that packet's originator.

canonical.quote: the order of the contents of a packet will be: local medium header, if used, Internet header, Datagram header, TFTP header
canonical.obligation: A transmitted packet places the TFTP header after the local medium, Internet and Datagram headers, followed by the TFTP payload.

canonical.quote: the source and destination port fields of the Datagram header ... are used by TFTP and the length field reflects the size
canonical.obligation: TFTP uses the datagram source/destination port fields, and the datagram length field reflects the TFTP packet size.

canonical.quote: The transfer identifiers (TID's) used by TFTP are passed to the Datagram layer to be used as ports
canonical.obligation: An implementation passes its TIDs to the datagram layer to be used as port numbers.

canonical.quote: therefore they must be between 0 and 65,535
canonical.obligation: A TID must be an integer in the range 0 to 65535.

canonical.quote: The TFTP header consists of a 2 byte opcode field which indicates the packet's type
canonical.obligation: Every TFTP packet begins with a 2-byte opcode field identifying its type.

canonical.quote: |  Local Medium  |  Internet  |  Datagram  |  TFTP  |
canonical.obligation: Header order on the wire is local medium, Internet, Datagram, then TFTP.

canonical.quote: A transfer is established by sending a request (WRQ to write onto a foreign file system, or RRQ to read from it)
canonical.obligation: A client establishes a transfer by sending WRQ to write to the remote file system or RRQ to read from it.

canonical.quote: receiving a positive reply, an acknowledgment packet for write, or the first data packet for read
canonical.obligation: The positive reply is an ACK for a write request and the first DATA packet for a read request.

canonical.quote: In general an acknowledgment packet will contain the block number of the data packet being acknowledged.
canonical.obligation: An ACK carries the block number of the DATA packet it acknowledges.

canonical.quote: Each data packet has associated with it a block number; block numbers are consecutive and begin with one.
canonical.obligation: DATA block numbers start at one and are consecutive.

canonical.quote: Since the positive response to a write request is an acknowledgment packet, in this special case the block number will be zero.
canonical.obligation: The ACK that positively answers a WRQ carries block number zero.

canonical.quote: If the reply is an error packet, then the request has been denied.
canonical.obligation: An ERROR packet in reply to a request means the request was denied.

canonical.quote: each end of the connection chooses a TID for itself, to be used for the duration of that connection
canonical.obligation: Each endpoint chooses one TID and keeps it for the whole connection.

canonical.quote: The TID's chosen for a connection should be randomly chosen, so that the probability that the same number is chosen twice
canonical.obligation: An implementation should choose TIDs randomly so immediate reuse is improbable.

canonical.quote: Every packet has associated with it the two TID's of the ends of the connection, the source TID and the destination TID.
canonical.obligation: Every packet carries a source TID and a destination TID identifying the two connection endpoints.

canonical.quote: These TID's are handed to the supporting UDP (or other datagram protocol) as the source and destination ports.
canonical.obligation: An implementation maps the source and destination TIDs onto the datagram source and destination ports.

canonical.quote: A requesting host chooses its source TID as described above
canonical.obligation: The requesting host selects its own source TID by the random-choice rule.

canonical.quote: sends its initial request to the known TID 69 decimal (105 octal) on the serving host
canonical.obligation: The initial RRQ/WRQ is addressed to destination TID 69 on the server.

canonical.quote: The response to the request, under normal operation, uses a TID chosen by the server as its source TID
canonical.obligation: The server answers the request from a newly chosen source TID rather than from TID 69.

canonical.quote: the TID chosen for the previous message by the requestor as its destination TID
canonical.obligation: The server's response is addressed to the requestor's source TID as destination TID.

canonical.quote: The two chosen TID's are then used for the remainder of the transfer.
canonical.obligation: Both endpoints use the agreed TID pair for the rest of the transfer.

canonical.quote: the first data packet can be sent by Host A with a sequence number of 1
canonical.obligation: After the WRQ/ACK exchange the writer sends its first DATA packet with block number 1.

canonical.quote: the hosts should make sure that the source TID matches the value that was agreed on in steps 1 and 2
canonical.obligation: On every received packet a host should check that the source TID matches the TID agreed during connection setup.

canonical.quote: If a source TID does not match, the packet should be discarded as erroneously sent from somewhere else.
canonical.obligation: A packet whose source TID does not match the connection must be discarded.

canonical.quote: An error packet should be sent to the source of the incorrect packet, while not disturbing the transfer.
canonical.obligation: An ERROR packet is sent to the originator of a wrong-TID packet without disturbing the ongoing transfer.

canonical.quote: TFTP supports five types of packets ... 1 Read request (RRQ) 2 Write request (WRQ) 3 Data (DATA) 4 Acknowledgment (ACK) 5 Error (ERROR)
canonical.obligation: Exactly five packet types exist with opcodes 1=RRQ, 2=WRQ, 3=DATA, 4=ACK, 5=ERROR.

canonical.quote: The TFTP header of a packet contains the opcode associated with that packet.
canonical.obligation: Each packet's TFTP header carries the opcode of that packet's type.

canonical.quote: 2 bytes  string  1 byte  string  1 byte | Opcode | Filename | 0 | Mode | 0 |
canonical.obligation: An RRQ/WRQ packet is a 2-byte opcode, a Filename string, a zero byte, a Mode string, and a zero byte in that order.

canonical.quote: RRQ and WRQ packets (opcodes 1 and 2 respectively) have the format shown in Figure 5-1.
canonical.obligation: RRQ uses opcode 1 and WRQ opcode 2, both with the Figure 5-1 layout.

canonical.quote: The file name is a sequence of bytes in netascii terminated by a zero byte.
canonical.obligation: The Filename field is netascii bytes terminated by a single zero byte.

canonical.quote: The mode field contains the string "netascii", "octet", or "mail" (or any combination of upper and lower case ...) in netascii
canonical.obligation: The Mode field is a netascii string equal to netascii, octet or mail, compared case-insensitively.

canonical.quote: A host which receives netascii mode data must translate the data to its own format.
canonical.obligation: A receiver in netascii mode must convert incoming netascii into its local text format.

canonical.quote: Octet mode is used to transfer a file that is in the 8-bit format of the machine from which the file is being transferred.
canonical.obligation: Octet mode transfers the file in the sending machine's native 8-bit format without translation.

canonical.quote: If a host receives a octet file and then returns it, the returned file must be identical to the original.
canonical.obligation: An octet-mode round trip must return a byte-identical file.

canonical.quote: Mail mode uses the name of a mail recipient in place of a file and must begin with a WRQ.
canonical.obligation: In mail mode the Filename field carries a recipient name and the transfer must start with a WRQ; superseded by the mail-mode deprecation and RFC 1123 4.2.2.1.

canonical.quote: The mail recipient string should be of the form "username" or "username@hostname".
canonical.obligation: A mail-mode recipient string should be username or username@hostname; superseded by the mail-mode deprecation.

canonical.quote: It is also possible to define other modes for cooperating pairs of hosts, although this must be done with care.
canonical.obligation: An implementation may define non-standard modes only by agreement between cooperating hosts and with care.

canonical.quote: 2 bytes  2 bytes  n bytes | Opcode | Block # | Data |
canonical.obligation: A DATA packet is a 2-byte opcode, a 2-byte block number, then n bytes of data.

canonical.quote: DATA packets (opcode = 3) have a block number and data field.
canonical.obligation: DATA uses opcode 3 and carries a block number field and a data field.

canonical.quote: The block numbers on data packets begin with one and increase by one for each new block of data.
canonical.obligation: DATA block numbers start at one and increment by one per new block.

canonical.quote: The data field is from zero to 512 bytes long.
canonical.obligation: The DATA data field length is between 0 and 512 bytes inclusive.

canonical.quote: If it is 512 bytes long, the block is not the last block of data
canonical.obligation: A full 512-byte data field means the transfer continues.

canonical.quote: if it is from zero to 511 bytes long, it signals the end of the transfer
canonical.obligation: A data field of 0 to 511 bytes signals the end of the transfer.

canonical.quote: All packets other than duplicate ACK's and those used for termination are acknowledged unless a timeout occurs [4].
canonical.obligation: Every packet except duplicate ACKs and termination packets is acknowledged, absent a timeout.

canonical.quote: Sending a DATA packet is an acknowledgment for the first ACK packet of the previous DATA packet.
canonical.obligation: Transmitting the next DATA packet implicitly acknowledges the first ACK of the previous DATA packet.

canonical.quote: The WRQ and DATA packets are acknowledged by ACK or ERROR packets
canonical.obligation: A WRQ or DATA packet is answered by an ACK or an ERROR packet.

canonical.quote: RRQ and ACK packets are acknowledged by DATA or ERROR packets
canonical.obligation: An RRQ or ACK packet is answered by a DATA or an ERROR packet.

canonical.quote: 2 bytes  2 bytes | Opcode | Block # |
canonical.obligation: An ACK packet is exactly a 2-byte opcode followed by a 2-byte block number.

canonical.quote: Figure 5-3 depicts an ACK packet; the opcode is 4.
canonical.obligation: ACK packets use opcode 4.

canonical.quote: The block number in an ACK echoes the block number of the DATA packet being acknowledged.
canonical.obligation: An ACK's block number equals the block number of the DATA packet it acknowledges.

canonical.quote: A WRQ is acknowledged with an ACK packet having a block number of zero.
canonical.obligation: The ACK answering a WRQ carries block number zero.

canonical.quote: 2 bytes  2 bytes  string  1 byte | Opcode | ErrorCode | ErrMsg | 0 |
canonical.obligation: An ERROR packet is a 2-byte opcode, a 2-byte error code, an ErrMsg string and a terminating zero byte.

canonical.quote: An ERROR packet (opcode 5) takes the form depicted in Figure 5-4.
canonical.obligation: ERROR packets use opcode 5 with the Figure 5-4 layout.

canonical.quote: An ERROR packet can be the acknowledgment of any other type of packet.
canonical.obligation: An ERROR packet is an admissible response to any packet type.

canonical.quote: The error code is an integer indicating the nature of the error.
canonical.obligation: The ErrorCode field is an integer selected from the defined error-code table.

canonical.quote: The error message is intended for human consumption, and should be in netascii.
canonical.obligation: The ErrMsg field should be netascii text meant for humans.

canonical.quote: Like all other strings, it is terminated with a zero byte.
canonical.obligation: The ErrMsg string, like every TFTP string, is terminated by a zero byte.

canonical.quote: The end of a transfer is marked by a DATA packet that contains between 0 and 511 bytes of data (i.e., Datagram length < 516).
canonical.obligation: A DATA packet with 0 to 511 data bytes marks the end of the transfer.

canonical.quote: This packet is acknowledged by an ACK packet like all other DATA packets.
canonical.obligation: The final DATA packet is acknowledged with an ACK exactly like any other DATA packet.

canonical.quote: The host acknowledging the final DATA packet may terminate its side of the connection on sending the final ACK.
canonical.obligation: The acknowledger may close its side of the connection immediately after sending the final ACK.

canonical.quote: dallying is encouraged.  This means that the host sending the final ACK will wait for a while before terminating
canonical.obligation: The acknowledger should dally after the final ACK so it can retransmit that ACK if it is lost.

canonical.quote: The acknowledger will know that the ACK has been lost if it receives the final DATA packet again.
canonical.obligation: A repeated final DATA packet tells the dallying acknowledger its final ACK was lost and must be resent.

canonical.quote: The host sending the last DATA must retransmit it until the packet is acknowledged or the sending host times out.
canonical.obligation: The sender of the last DATA packet must retransmit it until acknowledged or until it times out.

canonical.quote: If the response is an ACK, the transmission was completed successfully.
canonical.obligation: Receiving the ACK for the final DATA packet means the transfer completed successfully.

canonical.quote: In any case, the connection has been closed.
canonical.obligation: After the sender's final timeout the connection is considered closed regardless of outcome.

canonical.quote: If a request can not be granted, or some error occurs during the transfer, then an ERROR packet (opcode 5) is sent.
canonical.obligation: An implementation sends an ERROR packet when a request cannot be granted or an error occurs mid-transfer.

canonical.quote: This is only a courtesy since it will not be retransmitted or acknowledged
canonical.obligation: The ERROR packet is sent once: it is neither retransmitted nor acknowledged.

canonical.quote: Timeouts must also be used to detect errors.
canonical.obligation: An implementation must use timeouts to detect errors that no ERROR packet reports.

canonical.quote: | Local Medium | Internet | Datagram | TFTP Opcode |   (2 bytes)
canonical.obligation: The TFTP opcode is the first 2 bytes following the datagram header.

canonical.quote: RRQ/WRQ | 01/02 | Filename | 0 | Mode | 0 |
canonical.obligation: RRQ opcode 01 and WRQ opcode 02, each followed by Filename, zero byte, Mode, zero byte.

canonical.quote: DATA | 03 | Block # | Data |   2 bytes 2 bytes n bytes
canonical.obligation: DATA opcode 03 followed by a 2-byte block number and n data bytes.

canonical.quote: ACK | 04 | Block # |   2 bytes 2 bytes
canonical.obligation: ACK opcode 04 followed by a 2-byte block number and nothing else.

canonical.quote: ERROR | 05 | ErrorCode | ErrMsg | 0 |
canonical.obligation: ERROR opcode 05 followed by a 2-byte error code, an ErrMsg string and a zero byte.

canonical.quote: 0         Not defined, see error message (if any).
canonical.obligation: Error code 0 means an undefined error described only by the accompanying message.

canonical.quote: 1         File not found.
canonical.obligation: Error code 1 is returned when the requested file does not exist.

canonical.quote: 2         Access violation.
canonical.obligation: Error code 2 is returned when the requester lacks permission for the file.

canonical.quote: 3         Disk full or allocation exceeded.
canonical.obligation: Error code 3 is returned when storage is exhausted or a quota is exceeded.

canonical.quote: 4         Illegal TFTP operation.
canonical.obligation: Error code 4 is returned for a malformed or illegal TFTP operation.

canonical.quote: 5         Unknown transfer ID.
canonical.obligation: Error code 5 is returned to the source of a packet bearing an unknown transfer ID.

canonical.quote: 6         File already exists.
canonical.obligation: Error code 6 is returned when a write target already exists.

canonical.quote: 7         No such user.
canonical.obligation: Error code 7 is returned when a mail-mode recipient does not exist.

canonical.section: I. Appendix / Internet User Datagram Header
canonical.quote: TFTP need not be implemented on top of the Internet User Datagram Protocol.
canonical.obligation: An implementation is not obliged to use UDP as the underlying transport.

canonical.quote: Dest. Port      Picked by destination machine (69 for RRQ or WRQ).
canonical.obligation: The destination port for an initial RRQ or WRQ is 69; thereafter it is the peer's chosen TID.

canonical.quote: Length          Number of bytes in UDP packet, including UDP header.
canonical.obligation: The datagram length field counts the whole UDP packet including its 8-byte header; RFC 1123 4.2.2.2 confirms this against RFC 783.

canonical.quote: TFTP passes transfer identifiers (TID's) to the Internet User Datagram protocol to be used as the source and destination ports.
canonical.obligation: An implementation supplies its TIDs as the UDP source and destination port numbers.

canonical.quote: care must be taken in the rights granted to a TFTP server process so as not to violate the security
canonical.obligation: A deployment must restrict the file-system rights of the TFTP server process because TFTP has no login or access control.

canonical.quote: Vendors are urged to support TFTP for booting.
canonical.obligation: Host vendors are expected to provide TFTP so hosts can be bootstrapped over the network.

canonical.quote: The transfer mode "mail" SHOULD NOT be supported.
canonical.obligation: An implementation should not support the mail transfer mode; supersedes RFC 1350's mail-mode text.

canonical.quote: The Length field of a UDP header is incorrectly defined; it includes the UDP header length (8).
canonical.obligation: The UDP Length field includes the 8-byte UDP header, correcting RFC 783's definition.

canonical.quote: Implementations MUST contain the fix for this problem: the sender ... must never resend the current DATA packet on receipt of a duplicate ACK.
canonical.obligation: The DATA sender must never retransmit the current DATA packet in response to a duplicate ACK; overrides RFC 1350's may-retransmit-on-duplicate rule.

canonical.quote: A TFTP implementation MUST use an adaptive timeout.
canonical.obligation: An implementation must compute its retransmission timeout adaptively rather than using a fixed value.

canonical.quote: A server TFTP implementation SHOULD include some configurable access control over what pathnames are allowed in TFTP operations.
canonical.obligation: A server should provide configurable access control over which pathnames TFTP operations may touch.

canonical.quote: A TFTP request directed to a broadcast address SHOULD be silently ignored.
canonical.obligation: A server should discard a TFTP request that arrived on a broadcast address without replying.

canonical.quote: netascii                                       |RFC-783 |x| | | | |
canonical.obligation: An implementation must support the netascii transfer mode.

canonical.quote: octet                                          |RFC-783 |x| | | | |
canonical.obligation: An implementation must support the octet transfer mode.

canonical.quote: extensions                                     |4.2.3.3 | | |x| | |
canonical.obligation: An implementation may add non-standard TFTP extensions, none of which are standardized.

canonical.quote: One sends data and receives acknowledgments, the other sends acknowledgments and receives data.
canonical.obligation: Each transfer has two complementary roles: DATA sender/ACK receiver and ACK sender/DATA receiver.

canonical.quote: When the second response to the request arrives, it should be rejected, but there is no reason to terminate the first connection.
canonical.obligation: A second (duplicate-request) response is rejected while the first connection continues.

canonical.quote: Source Port     Picked by originator of packet.
canonical.obligation: The source port of each packet is the TID picked by the packet's originator.

canonical.quote: (The implementor of this should be sure that the correct algorithm is used here.) Field contains zero if unused.
canonical.obligation: The implementor should compute the datagram checksum with the correct algorithm, or send zero when unused.

canonical.quote: A variety of non-standard extensions have been made to TFTP ... None of these have been standardized.
canonical.obligation: TFTP extensions are non-standard and optional; an implementation need not support any of them.
